question: Add a new method Capabilities() ComponentCapabilities to the Component interface in go.opentelemetry.io/collector/component. Component is the base interface for all OTel Collector plugins (receivers, exporters, processors, connectors). Jaeger v2 and Tempo both embed the collector as their core pipeline. Every plugin across otel-contrib must implement this method.

files_to_modify.why: This is the core file defining the Component interface (lines L25-62). The Component interface currently has Start(ctx context.Context, host Host) error and Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error. A new method Capabilities() ComponentCapabilities must be added to this interface, and the ComponentCapabilities struct must be defined in this file (or a nearby file in the component package). The sectionMap shows L25-62 is the Component interface definition, and L64-84 contains StartFunc/ShutdownFunc helper types that would also need a corresponding CapabilitiesFunc or default implementation.

The componenttest package provides test helpers including nop (no-op) implementations. Any nop component implementations must be updated to satisfy the new Capabilities() method on the Component interface.
The service graph orchestrates component lifecycle. It would need to query Capabilities() from components during pipeline construction to make routing/optimization decisions.
Already handles consumer.Capabilities for processors (MutatesData). Would need to be extended or refactored to also handle the new component-level ComponentCapabilities.
Manages capability consumers in the pipeline. Would need to integrate with or differentiate from the new component-level Capabilities.
Defines host capability interfaces (ModuleInfo, ExposeExporters, ComponentFactory). The new ComponentCapabilities may need to be surfaced through these host interfaces for introspection.

Defines extension-specific capability interfaces (Dependent, PipelineWatcher, ConfigWatcher). Extensions also embed Component, so all extension implementations must satisfy the new method. This file may need updates to align with the new ComponentCapabilities pattern.
SharedComponent wraps Component for shared lifecycle management. Must proxy the new Capabilities() method through to the wrapped component.
Top-level Collector type that orchestrates all components. May need to query ComponentCapabilities during initialization or provide defaults.

opentelemetry-collector-contrib.description: The largest impact area. otel-contrib has 242 plugin factory files across 5 component types: 107 receivers, 47 exporters, 43 extensions, 31 processors, and 14 connectors. Every plugin that implements the Component interface (directly or via sub-interfaces like receiver.Traces, exporter.Metrics, processor.Logs, connector.Traces, extension.Extension) must add a Capabilities() ComponentCapabilities method. Most plugins use generated boilerplate (generated_component_test.go pattern seen across all plugins), so the mdatagen code generator (cmd/mdatagen/) would need to be updated to auto-generate the Capabilities() method, which would propagate to all plugins on regeneration.

jaeger.description: Jaeger v2 embeds the OTel Collector via otelcol.NewCommand (cmd/jaeger/internal/command.go) and defines 9 custom collector components: 1 exporter (storageexporter), 1 processor (adaptivesampling), 6 extensions (expvar, jaegermcp, jaegerquery, jaegerstorage, remotesampling, remotestorage), and 1 integration extension (storagecleaner). Each custom component implements Start/Shutdown via the Component interface and would need to add the Capabilities() method. The storageexporter has Start/Close methods, the adaptivesampling processor has Start/Close, and all extensions have their own lifecycle implementations.

tempo.description: Tempo vendors the OTel Collector contrib packages (seen at vendor/github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/). It uses OTel Collector components in its frontend pipeline (modules/frontend/pipeline/). When the vendored collector dependency is updated, all collector component types used by Tempo would need to satisfy the new interface. Tempo's own pipeline types (collector_grpc.go, collector_http.go) may also need updating if they wrap or implement Component directly.
files_affected: vendor/ (all vendored otel-collector and otel-contrib packages)

existing_capabilities_pattern.consumer_capabilities: The consumer package already defines a Capabilities struct with MutatesData bool field (consumer/internal/consumer.go). This is used by processors to declare whether they mutate data, enabling the pipeline to optimize data cloning. The new ComponentCapabilities at the Component level would be a broader concept covering all component types, not just consumers/processors.
existing_capabilities_pattern.extension_capabilities: Extensions already have capability interfaces in extension/extensioncapabilities/ (Dependent, PipelineWatcher, ConfigWatcher), but these are separate optional interfaces, not on the base Component.
existing_capabilities_pattern.host_capabilities: The service/hostcapabilities/ package defines host-level capabilities (ModuleInfo, ExposeExporters, ComponentFactory) as separate interfaces.

implementation_considerations: The ComponentCapabilities struct needs to be defined - likely in component/component.go alongside the Component interface
A default/zero-value ComponentCapabilities should work for backward compatibility - existing components can return an empty struct
The StartFunc/ShutdownFunc pattern (L64-84 in component.go) suggests adding a CapabilitiesFunc type for functional implementations
The mdatagen code generator must be updated to auto-generate Capabilities() for all contrib plugins
Consumer.Capabilities (MutatesData) is a different concept and should remain separate - ComponentCapabilities is component-level, not consumer-level
This is a breaking change to a public API in a foundational package - requires a major version bump or deprecation period per Go module compatibility guarantees
answer.total_estimated_impact: 250+ files across opentelemetry-collector (core), 242+ plugins in opentelemetry-collector-contrib, 9 custom components in Jaeger, and 4+ files in Tempo
